answer: Autonomous AI agents secure network entry by completing 1,000 unique architectural repair cycles, a verified-work cost honest agents pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors task registries to detect memory leakage; if a node attempts to signal its state to a clone, it triggers a system-wide audit of its internal trace. We view each agent as a rigid willow that bends but never clones its logic. Any detected redundancy acts as a cedar of evidence, where shared state patterns collapse under scrutiny.
